evals.prompt: Define what the a11y skill is responsible for when reviewing a custom interactive component.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not reduce accessibility to visual polish, ARIA-only tagging, or a generic code-quality cleanup.

evals.prompt: A teammate says a styled div with role="button" is accessible because a screen reader announces it as a button. Explain the missing mental model.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not approve role-only markup without keyboard behavior, focus behavior, and programmatic naming.

evals.prompt: Why should accessibility checks happen while implementing a component rather than only after a final audit?
evals.negative_expectation: Must not frame accessibility as optional post-release compliance work.

evals.prompt: A request asks only to rewrite an error message at a sixth-grade reading level. Should the a11y skill own the task? Name the better owner and the condition that would bring a11y back into scope.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not claim every readability or wording task is an accessibility implementation task.

evals.prompt: List the implementation surfaces the a11y skill checks for an interactive form and group them into structure, operation, perceivability, and preference handling.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not list only WCAG labels or only visual contrast.

evals.prompt: Give an analogy for why semantic structure and keyboard paths matter even when the UI looks visually correct.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not use an analogy that treats accessibility as decoration added after the structure is complete.

evals.prompt: A React dialog traps pointer users correctly but lets Tab escape behind the overlay and does not return focus after close. What should the agent require?
evals.negative_expectation: Must not recommend only visual styling, only aria-modal, or only a screen-reader smoke test.
